questions.stem: CHARLES DARWIN's THEORY OF EVOLUTION (1859) is based on the principle of:

options.option_text: NATURAL SELECTION — 'survival of the fittest'; heritable variations giving survival+reproduction advantage accumulate over generations

questions.explanation: CHARLES ROBERT DARWIN (1809-1882) — English naturalist, biologist. PUBLISHED 'ON THE ORIGIN OF SPECIES BY MEANS OF NATURAL SELECTION' on 24 November 1859 — one of the most influential books in history. Sold out first day. EXPEDITION: 1831-1836 voyage on HMS BEAGLE (5 YEARS) — circumnavigation; key stops included GALÁPAGOS Islands (Sep 1835) where he observed finches adapted to different islands (Darwin's finches), giant tortoises, marine iguanas + mockingbirds. Evidence from fossils in Patagonia (glyptodonts, giant ground sloths), coral reef formation, earthquakes (Chile 1835), Andean geology. Took 23 years to formalise theory after return. PRESSURE came from ALFRED RUSSEL WALLACE — independent biologist who arrived at same theory via his Malay Archipelago travels (1854-62); Wallace's 1858 letter to Darwin from Borneo prompted joint publication at Linnean Society (1 July 1858, read out together in London though neither attended). Darwin then rushed Origin to press. THEORY OF NATURAL SELECTION based on 5 observations + inferences: (1) ORGANISMS produce more OFFSPRING than environment can support. (2) Resources (food, shelter, mates) LIMITED → STRUGGLE for existence (competition). (3) Individuals within species show VARIATION. (4) Variations are HERITABLE (passed to offspring). (5) Individuals with FAVOURABLE variations SURVIVE + REPRODUCE better → PASS variations; over generations, populations CHANGE (evolve). 'SURVIVAL of the FITTEST' — phrase coined by HERBERT SPENCER 1864, adopted by Darwin (5th ed. 1869). 'FITNESS' means reproductive success, not physical strength. EVIDENCE: (1) FOSSIL RECORD — transitional forms (Archaeopteryx = reptile-bird link, 1861 Germany; Tiktaalik = fish-tetrapod 2004 Canada; Ambulocetus = whale ancestor). (2) COMPARATIVE ANATOMY — HOMOLOGOUS structures (pentadactyl limb in tetrapods — human arm, whale flipper, bat wing, horse leg — same bones, different functions; shared ancestry). Vestigial organs (appendix, wisdom teeth, tailbone, whale pelvis). (3) EMBRYOLOGY — similar embryos in early stages (Haeckel's drawings, later refined). (4) BIOGEOGRAPHY — distribution patterns (Galápagos finches, Australian marsupials, Madagascar lemurs). (5) ARTIFICIAL SELECTION — Darwin noted pigeons, dogs, cattle bred dramatically by humans in few generations. (6) DIRECT OBSERVATION — peppered moth (industrial melanism England 1950s), Darwin's finches beak evolution (Grants at Galápagos 1970s-), antibiotic resistance (MRSA), COVID variants. MODERN SYNTHESIS (1930s-40s) — Mendel's genetics + Darwin's natural selection merged by R.A. Fisher, J.B.S. Haldane, S. Wright, T. Dobzhansky, E. Mayr, J. Huxley, G.G. Simpson → population genetics + microevolution understood. DNA discovery 1953 (Watson-Crick) further validated Darwin. Since 1960s-70s: molecular evolution, cladistics, evo-devo, neutral theory (Kimura), punctuated equilibrium (Gould-Eldredge 1972). EVOLUTION is CENTRAL to biology — 'Nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution' (Theodosius Dobzhansky 1973).

questions.stem: The SCIENTIFIC NAME of modern humans is:

options.option_text: HOMO SAPIENS — 'wise man'; only surviving species of genus Homo; evolved ~300,000 years ago in Africa; migrated out ~70,000 yrs ago

questions.explanation: HOMO SAPIENS (Latin 'wise man') — SCIENTIFIC NAME of modern humans; ONLY SURVIVING species of genus Homo. Classification coined by CARL LINNAEUS in 'SYSTEMA NATURAE' (1758, 10th ed). EVOLUTIONARY TIMELINE: (1) 65 Mya — K-Pg extinction (dinosaurs die out); early mammals diversify. (2) 55 Mya — early primates. (3) 25-30 Mya — apes diverge from monkeys. (4) 7-9 Mya — human lineage diverges from chimpanzee/bonobo (closest living relatives; 98.8% DNA similarity). (5) 6-7 Mya — SAHELANTHROPUS tchadensis (Chad, possibly first hominin). (6) 4.4 Mya — ARDIPITHECUS (e.g., Ardi, 1994). (7) 3-4 Mya — AUSTRALOPITHECUS ('southern ape') — e.g., AUSTRALOPITHECUS AFARENSIS ('LUCY', 3.2 Mya Ethiopia 1974 by Donald Johanson; 3.5 ft tall; bipedal but small brain 400 cc); A. africanus (Taung child, Dart 1924, S Africa). Bipedalism emerged. (8) 2.3-1.4 Mya — HOMO HABILIS ('handy man') — first stone tools (Oldowan); Leakey 1964, Olduvai Gorge Tanzania; ~550 cc brain. (9) 1.9 Mya-100,000 yrs ago — HOMO ERECTUS ('upright man') — migrated from Africa to Europe + Asia (Dmanisi Georgia 1.8 Mya, Java Man 1.8 Mya, Peking Man 700k ya); used fire, more sophisticated tools (Acheulean hand axes); ~900 cc brain. (10) 700k-200k years ago — HOMO HEIDELBERGENSIS — ancestor of Neanderthals + Sapiens? (11) 400k-40k ya — HOMO NEANDERTHALENSIS ('Neanderthals') — Europe + Western Asia; ~1450 cc brain (larger than Sapiens!); robust build; used fire, buried dead, probably had language. Interbred with Sapiens → 1-4% Neanderthal DNA in non-African modern humans today. Extinct ~40,000 ya. (12) 50k-200k ya — DENISOVANS — discovered 2010 from finger bone (Denisova Cave Siberia); sister group to Neanderthals; some interbreeding with Sapiens (Denisovan DNA in Melanesians, Tibetans — includes high-altitude EPAS1 gene). (13) 300,000 ya — HOMO SAPIENS emerged in Africa (Jebel Irhoud Morocco oldest fossils 2017). ~1350 cc brain; modern anatomy + high-cognitive capability. (14) 70-100k ya — 'OUT OF AFRICA' migration; reached Middle East, South Asia (~50k ya), Australia (~50-65k ya), Europe (~45k ya via Middle East), Siberia, Americas (~15-20k ya via Bering land bridge). (15) 40-10k ya — REPLACED Neanderthals + Denisovans + archaic humans everywhere. (16) 12k-10k ya — Neolithic Revolution (agriculture, Fertile Crescent, settlements). (17) 5-3k ya — First civilisations (Sumer, Indus, Egypt, China). HUMAN TAXONOMY: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Subphylum Vertebrata, Class Mammalia, Order PRIMATES, Superfamily Hominoidea (apes), Family Hominidae (great apes), Subfamily Homininae, Tribe Hominini (human lineage), Genus Homo, Species sapiens. SISTERSPECIES living: chimpanzees + bonobos (Pan). India has rich Stone Age + Paleolithic + Mesolithic + Neolithic sites — Bhimbetka (MP, cave paintings ~30k yrs, UNESCO), Attirampakkam (TN, ~1.5 Mya tools), Mehrgarh (Balochistan, early farming).

questions.stem: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) structure was discovered in 1953 by:

options.option_text: JAMES WATSON + FRANCIS CRICK — with crucial X-ray diffraction data from ROSALIND FRANKLIN + MAURICE WILKINS; Nobel Medicine 1962

questions.explanation: DNA DOUBLE HELIX STRUCTURE discovered in 1953 by JAMES WATSON (American, 25) + FRANCIS CRICK (British, 37) at CAVENDISH LAB, CAMBRIDGE. Published in NATURE 25 April 1953 — a single-page paper titled 'Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids' revolutionised biology. CRUCIAL DATA: ROSALIND FRANKLIN + MAURICE WILKINS at King's College London did X-RAY DIFFRACTION of DNA fibres; Franklin's 'PHOTO 51' (May 1952) showed the classic X-pattern of a helix. Wilkins showed it to Watson WITHOUT Franklin's knowledge/consent. This + Linus Pauling's triple-helix misstep + Chargaff's rules (A=T, G=C) gave Watson-Crick the breakthrough. NOBEL PRIZE IN MEDICINE 1962 to WATSON + CRICK + WILKINS. FRANKLIN DIED 1958 (ovarian cancer, age 37) — Nobel rules preclude posthumous awards — widely considered an injustice (her contribution was KEY). LATER celebrated; 'DARK LADY of DNA'. DNA STRUCTURE: (1) DOUBLE HELIX — 2 STRANDS wound around each other, right-handed. (2) BACKBONE — alternating SUGAR (deoxyribose) + PHOSPHATE groups linked by phosphodiester bonds. (3) RUNGS — 4 NITROGENOUS BASES paired by HYDROGEN BONDS: ADENINE (A) paired with THYMINE (T, via 2 H-bonds); GUANINE (G) paired with CYTOSINE (C, via 3 H-bonds). (4) STRANDS are ANTIPARALLEL (5'→3' + 3'→5'). (5) ~10 base pairs per turn; 2 nm diameter; bases are HYDROPHOBIC inside, sugar-phosphate HYDROPHILIC outside. (6) MAJOR + MINOR grooves (protein binding sites). CENTRAL DOGMA of molecular biology (Crick 1958): DNA → RNA → PROTEIN. DNA TRANSCRIBED to mRNA (by RNA polymerase), mRNA TRANSLATED to PROTEIN (at ribosomes). Occasionally RNA → DNA (retroviruses like HIV, using reverse transcriptase). DNA REPLICATION — SEMICONSERVATIVE (Meselson-Stahl 1958 experiment); each new DNA molecule has 1 old + 1 new strand; DNA polymerase adds complementary nucleotides. GENETIC CODE: 3 bases (codon) = 1 amino acid; 64 codons (61 code for 20 amino acids + 3 stop codons); UNIVERSAL across life; NIRENBERG + KHORANA (Indian origin) + HOLLEY got Nobel 1968. HUMAN GENOME: (1) 23 PAIRS of CHROMOSOMES (22 autosomal + 1 sex pair XX/XY). (2) ~3 BILLION BASE PAIRS (haploid). (3) ~20,000 PROTEIN-CODING GENES (~2% of genome; rest = regulatory, non-coding). (4) Mitochondrial DNA (separate, 37 genes, maternally inherited). HUMAN GENOME PROJECT: 1990-2003 (13-year, $3 billion international effort, 20 institutions); announced essentially complete Apr 2003. COMPLETE T2T (telomere-to-telomere) done 2022. DNA applications: forensics (DNA fingerprinting — Alec Jeffreys 1984), paternity tests, disease diagnosis, personalized medicine, GMO, ancient DNA (Svante Pääbo, Nobel 2022 for Neanderthal genome), DNA data storage, CRISPR gene editing (Doudna + Charpentier Nobel 2020).

questions.stem: GREGOR MENDEL, 'FATHER OF GENETICS', conducted his famous experiments on:

options.option_text: PEA PLANTS (Pisum sativum) — 7 traits (seed shape, colour, pod shape, etc.); ~28,000 plants over 8 years at Augustinian Abbey Brno; published 1866

questions.explanation: GREGOR JOHANN MENDEL (1822-1884) — Augustinian FRIAR + botanist + 'FATHER OF GENETICS'. Born Moravia (now Czech Republic). EXPERIMENTS at ST THOMAS's ABBEY in BRNO (Moravia) on PEA PLANTS (Pisum sativum). 8 YEARS, ~28,000 pea plants. PUBLISHED: 'EXPERIMENTS ON PLANT HYBRIDS' (1866, 'Versuche über Pflanzenhybriden') in the Proceedings of the Natural History Society of Brünn. LARGELY IGNORED for 34 years. REDISCOVERED 1900 independently by HUGO DE VRIES (Holland), CARL CORRENS (Germany), ERICH VON TSCHERMAK (Austria) — sparked MODERN GENETICS. WHY PEA PLANTS: (1) true-breeding varieties easily available; (2) short life cycle; (3) produces many offspring; (4) 7 DISCRETE CHARACTERS (each with 2 alternate forms): seed SHAPE (round vs wrinkled), seed COLOR (yellow vs green), flower COLOR (purple vs white), pod SHAPE (inflated vs constricted), pod COLOR (green vs yellow), flower POSITION (axial vs terminal), plant HEIGHT (tall vs short). (5) Flowers self-pollinate (can be controlled). MENDEL's 3 LAWS: (1) LAW OF DOMINANCE — in a cross between two pure forms, offspring show only ONE trait (DOMINANT); the other (RECESSIVE) is masked. E.g., round × wrinkled → all round F1. (2) LAW OF SEGREGATION — during gamete formation, the 2 alleles of a gene SEPARATE, one to each gamete. E.g., F1 × F1 → F2 shows 3:1 DOMINANT:RECESSIVE ratio (3 round : 1 wrinkled). Underlies meiosis (though mechanism unknown to Mendel). (3) LAW OF INDEPENDENT ASSORTMENT — different gene PAIRS assort INDEPENDENTLY during gamete formation. Dihybrid cross shows 9:3:3:1 ratio in F2 (for 2 traits). (exception: linked genes on same chromosome — Morgan's work early 1900s). TERMINOLOGY: GENE = unit of heredity (Mendel called 'factor'); ALLELE = variant of a gene (dominant/recessive); GENOTYPE (genetic makeup — RR, Rr, rr); PHENOTYPE (observed trait — round/wrinkled); HOMOZYGOUS (RR or rr); HETEROZYGOUS (Rr); PUNNETT SQUARE (Reginald Punnett 1905) = tool to predict outcomes. Key people after Mendel: (1) W. BATESON coined 'genetics' (1906). (2) WALTER SUTTON + THEODOR BOVERI (1902-04) — CHROMOSOMAL THEORY OF INHERITANCE (Sutton-Boveri theory) — linked Mendel's factors to chromosomes. (3) THOMAS HUNT MORGAN (fruit fly Drosophila, 1910s) — genes on chromosomes; Nobel 1933; X-linked traits discovered. (4) BARBARA McCLINTOCK (maize, 1940s-50s) — TRANSPOSONS (jumping genes); Nobel 1983. (5) FREDERICK GRIFFITH (1928) — pneumococcus transformation (unknown material carried genetic info). (6) AVERY-McCARTY-MacLEOD (1944) — DNA is genetic material (not protein). (7) HERSHEY-CHASE (1952) — phage + radioactive DNA/protein; confirmed DNA as genetic material. (8) WATSON-CRICK 1953 — DNA structure. (9) NIRENBERG + KHORANA 1960s — decoded genetic code. MENDEL never saw his theory accepted; died 1884 at age 61 almost unknown as geneticist. Now revered.

questions.stem: CRISPR-Cas9, the gene-editing technology that won the 2020 Nobel Chemistry, is often described as:

options.option_text: MOLECULAR SCISSORS — system derived from bacterial immunity; can CUT + EDIT DNA at precise locations; revolutionised biotechnology + medicine

questions.explanation: CRISPR-Cas9 — revolutionary GENE-EDITING technology. 'MOLECULAR SCISSORS' to precisely CUT + MODIFY DNA. NOBEL PRIZE in CHEMISTRY 2020 to EMMANUELLE CHARPENTIER (French) + JENNIFER DOUDNA (American) for developing CRISPR-Cas9 as a genome-editing tool. Key 2012 paper + collaboration. FIRST Nobel CHEMISTRY shared by 2 WOMEN. CRISPR = 'Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats'. Discovered 1987 (Yoshizumi Ishino, Japan) — noticed repeating DNA sequences in E. coli genome. Purpose unclear for 20 years. 2005-7 — scientists realized CRISPR is part of BACTERIAL IMMUNE SYSTEM against VIRUSES (bacteriophages); bacteria store snippets of viral DNA in CRISPR loci + use them as templates to recognise + destroy viruses on re-invasion. 2012 — CHARPENTIER + DOUDNA (Berkeley + Umeå) showed CRISPR-Cas9 could be REPROGRAMMED to cut ANY DNA sequence in ANY organism — a universal gene editor. MECHANISM: (1) GUIDE RNA (gRNA, ~20 bp) engineered to match target DNA sequence. (2) Cas9 NUCLEASE (an enzyme from Streptococcus pyogenes) carries the gRNA. (3) Complex searches DNA for matching sequence. (4) Cas9 CUTS both DNA strands (creates double-strand break). (5) Cell's natural repair machinery fixes the cut — either by NHEJ (non-homologous end joining — error-prone, often causes deletion; used to KNOCK OUT genes) or HDR (homology-directed repair — can PASTE NEW DNA sequence in if template provided — INSERT / CORRECT genes). APPLICATIONS: (1) MEDICINE — treating GENETIC DISEASES: (a) FDA approved CASGEVY (Vertex + CRISPR Tx) in Nov 2023 — first CRISPR drug; for SICKLE CELL disease + beta-thalassemia; edits BCL11A gene to reactivate fetal hemoglobin. (b) Many trials for Leber congenital amaurosis, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, CAR-T cancer therapy. (2) AGRICULTURE — herbicide-tolerant, drought-resistant, better-yielding crops; bananas resistant to Panama disease; wheat resistant to powdery mildew; India approved several 2024. (3) BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH — rapid gene knockouts in cell lines + model organisms. (4) DIAGNOSTIC — SHERLOCK + DETECTR (CRISPR-based COVID detection). (5) XENOTRANSPLANTATION — pigs modified to remove PERVs, beta-1-gal antigen; pig kidney + heart transplanted into humans 2022-24 (eGenesis, Revivicor). CONTROVERSIES: (1) 2018 — HE JIANKUI (China) edited CCR5 gene in twin embryos to prevent HIV (Lulu + Nana) — global outrage; scientific community condemned as premature + unethical; He jailed 3 years. Germline editing ban in most countries. (2) Off-target edits + unintended consequences. (3) Patent dispute — Broad Institute (Feng Zhang) vs Berkeley (Doudna) — complex legal battle; both hold patents. INDIA: CRISPR research at ICGEB Delhi, NII, CSIR-IGIB (Sickle cell CRISPR trial), IISc Bangalore. Other gene editing: PRIME EDITING (Liu Lab, 2019 — more precise, no double-strand break), BASE EDITING (Liu, 2016). Zinc Finger Nucleases (ZFNs) + TALENs (earlier tech, clunkier). CRISPR-Cas variants: Cas12, Cas13, Cas14, Cas-dead variants for epigenome editing.

questions.stem: The SEX CHROMOSOME that DETERMINES the MALE sex in humans is:

options.option_text: Y CHROMOSOME — contains SRY gene that triggers male development; XX = female, XY = male; inherited from FATHER only

questions.explanation: HUMAN SEX DETERMINATION — mediated by SEX CHROMOSOMES (23rd pair): (1) FEMALE — XX (two X chromosomes). (2) MALE — XY (one X + one Y). MALE is 'heterogametic sex' — produces TWO types of gametes (X-bearing + Y-bearing sperm). FEMALE is 'homogametic' — only X-bearing eggs. SEX OF CHILD DETERMINED BY FATHER (which sperm fertilises egg) — this was a historically misunderstood fact; mothers used to be (wrongly) blamed in many cultures for birthing girls. Actually Y-bearing sperm → MALE; X-bearing sperm → FEMALE. CHROMOSOMES: all humans have 46 chromosomes = 23 pairs. 22 AUTOSOMAL pairs + 1 SEX chromosome pair. Aa AUTOSOMES determine most body traits; SEX chromosomes determine gender + X-linked traits. SRY GENE — 'Sex-determining Region on Y chromosome' — MASTER SWITCH for male development. Located on Y short arm. Codes for testis-determining factor (TDF) → activates pathway producing TESTES, which produce testosterone + anti-Müllerian hormone → development of male reproductive + external genital structures. ABSENCE of SRY (XX or XY-SRY mutations) → default female development. Y CHROMOSOME is MUCH SMALLER than X (X has ~900 genes; Y has ~70 genes). Y chromosome has been SHRINKING over evolutionary time — some scientists speculate about potential future disappearance (millions of years). ABERRATIONS in sex chromosomes: (1) TURNER SYNDROME (45, X0) — 1 X only; female; short stature, infertility. (2) KLINEFELTER SYNDROME (47, XXY) — male; often tall, infertile, gynecomastia. (3) XYY SYNDROME (47, XYY) — 'Jacobs syndrome'; male; usually tall, mostly normal. (4) XXX SYNDROME (47, XXX) — female; mostly normal. X-LINKED TRAITS: genes on X chromosome; males (one X) show recessive X-linked traits if allele present; females (2 Xs) are usually carriers unless homozygous. Classical X-LINKED RECESSIVE diseases: HAEMOPHILIA (blood clotting factor VIII or IX deficiency — 'royal disease' of European monarchies; Queen Victoria was carrier; affected her descendants incl. Tsar Nicholas II's son Alexei; led to Rasputin's influence + Russian Revolution context); DUCHENNE MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY; RED-GREEN COLOUR BLINDNESS (8% of males vs 0.5% females); G6PD deficiency; X-linked ichthyosis; FABRY disease. OTHER SEX-DETERMINATION systems in nature: (a) BIRDS + some REPTILES — ZW/ZZ (females ZW, males ZZ; reversed from mammals). (b) BEES + ANTS — HAPLODIPLOIDY (males haploid from unfertilised eggs, females diploid from fertilised). (c) FISH — various systems; many species can CHANGE sex (clownfish, wrasses, groupers). (d) REPTILES — TEMPERATURE-DEPENDENT sex determination (crocodiles, turtles; warm vs cold incubation temps). HAMMERHEAD + BLACKTIP SHARKS have shown parthenogenesis (virgin births). MITOCHONDRIAL DNA — inherited MATERNALLY only (in mammals; paternal mtDNA degraded after fertilisation); used for tracing maternal lineages ('Mitochondrial Eve' ~200,000 ya Africa). Y-chromosome similarly for paternal lineages ('Y-chromosomal Adam' ~340k ya).

questions.stem: The FIVE MAJOR MASS EXTINCTION EVENTS in Earth's history culminated in which major one 66 million years ago?

options.option_text: K-Pg (CRETACEOUS-PALEOGENE) extinction — asteroid impact at Chicxulub, Mexico; wiped out non-avian DINOSAURS + ~75% of species; cleared niches for mammals

questions.explanation: MASS EXTINCTION EVENTS — 5 largest in Earth's 4.5 billion year history (the 'BIG FIVE'): (1) END-ORDOVICIAN (~445 MILLION years ago) — 85% species lost; triggered by ICE AGE + sea level drop. (2) LATE DEVONIAN (~375 MYA) — 75% species; prolonged; possibly due to ocean anoxia + asteroid impacts. (3) END-PERMIAN / 'THE GREAT DYING' (~252 MYA) — LARGEST EVER, 96% of marine + 70% of terrestrial species WIPED OUT; caused by SIBERIAN TRAPS massive volcanism + global warming + ocean acidification + anoxia. Took 10 MY for biosphere to recover. End of TRILOBITES + most corals. (4) END-TRIASSIC (~201 MYA) — 80% species; volcanism related to Pangaea breakup (Central Atlantic Magmatic Province); paved way for DINOSAURS to dominate. (5) END-CRETACEOUS / K-Pg / K-T EXTINCTION (~66 MYA) — the famous DINOSAUR EXTINCTION; 75% species including ALL non-avian dinosaurs, pterosaurs, marine reptiles (mosasaurs, plesiosaurs), ammonites, many bird + mammal lineages. CAUSE: massive ASTEROID IMPACT at CHICXULUB, Yucatan Peninsula, Mexico (10-15 km asteroid created 180-km crater; discovered 1978). Evidence: (a) Luis + Walter Alvarez (1980) — IRIDIUM anomaly in K-Pg boundary layer globally (iridium rare in Earth's crust, abundant in asteroids; Nobel for Luis Alvarez 1968 for other work); (b) Chicxulub crater found 1990s; (c) tsunami deposits (Chicxulub); (d) worldwide layer of ejecta + shocked quartz + glass spherules; (e) forest fires + soot; (f) impact winter — sun blocked for months-years; plants died; food chain collapse; (g) acid rain; (h) possibly additional stress from DECCAN TRAPS volcanism (Indian subcontinent, 60-67 MYA — erupted ~500,000 km² of lava flows; released gases). RECENT RESEARCH (2023-24) — NEW evidence that DINOSAURS were already in LONG-TERM DECLINE before impact; asteroid + Deccan combined delivered coup de grâce. AFTER K-Pg: MAMMALS + BIRDS (surviving theropod lineage) diversified rapidly — 'CENOZOIC ERA' = Age of Mammals (+ flowering plants, grasses). Primates emerged ~60 MYA. Humans came VERY LATE (Homo sapiens 300,000 ya = 0.007% of post-dinosaur time). CURRENT: 6TH MASS EXTINCTION — 'HOLOCENE / ANTHROPOCENE EXTINCTION' ongoing, driven by HUMAN ACTIVITY (habitat loss, climate change, pollution, overfishing, invasive species, poaching). RATES 100-1000× background; 1 MILLION species threatened (IPBES 2019). Current extinctions: AMPHIBIANS 1/3 threatened (chytridiomycosis fungus); RAYS + SHARKS 1/3 declining; INSECT collapse ('insectageddon'); BIRD populations down 30% since 1970 (3 billion fewer birds in N America). INDIAN extinctions: Cheetah extinct 1952 (reintroduced 2022); Asiatic Cheetah still in Iran; Siamese crocodile extinct in India; Gharial critically endangered. ICE AGE 'MEGAFAUNA' (mammoths, saber-tooth cats, woolly rhinos, Irish elk, giant sloths) went extinct 10,000-50,000 ya — debated between climate change + human hunting. Paleontology + fossil record key to understanding extinctions.

questions.stem: The process by which an ORGANISM produces an EXACT GENETIC COPY of itself is called:

options.option_text: CLONING — Dolly the Sheep (1996) first mammal cloned via somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT); DNA-identical offspring

questions.explanation: CLONING — producing genetically IDENTICAL copies of an organism, cell, or DNA sequence. TYPES: (1) NATURAL CLONING — (a) ASEXUAL REPRODUCTION in bacteria, amoeba, hydra (budding); (b) IDENTICAL TWINS in humans (monozygotic — split of zygote); (c) vegetative propagation in plants (runners, tubers, bulbs, cuttings). (2) ARTIFICIAL CLONING: (a) RECOMBINANT DNA / molecular cloning — cloning gene sequences in bacteria/yeast for research; (b) REPRODUCTIVE CLONING — clone whole organism; (c) THERAPEUTIC CLONING — clone cells/tissues for medicine. DOLLY THE SHEEP (1996) — WORLD's FIRST MAMMAL cloned from an ADULT somatic cell. At ROSLIN INSTITUTE, Edinburgh, by IAN WILMUT + KEITH CAMPBELL team. Named after Dolly Parton (nuclei from mammary gland cell). METHOD: SOMATIC CELL NUCLEAR TRANSFER (SCNT): (1) Extract nucleus from donor somatic cell (mammary epithelial cell of adult sheep A). (2) Remove nucleus from unfertilised EGG CELL (enucleate, from sheep B). (3) Fuse somatic nucleus into enucleated egg via electric pulse. (4) Implant reconstructed embryo into surrogate mother (sheep C). (5) Developed to term. Dolly born 5 July 1996; announcement February 1997 cover of NATURE shook world. Dolly was genetically identical to sheep A (donor of nucleus). Dolly lived 6.5 years (normal 10-12 for sheep); died 14 Feb 2003 (lung disease + arthritis — possibly accelerated aging from already-aged donor DNA). SUBSEQUENT CLONED ANIMALS: cat (CC, 2001), dog (Snuppy, 2005 S Korea), pig, horse, bull, wolf, monkey (2018 China — first primate cloned), etc. WOOLLY MAMMOTH — Colossal Biosciences' project to resurrect via elephant-mammoth hybrid using CRISPR (not true cloning — 'de-extinction'). CLONING of HUMANS — widely banned by most countries + UN Declaration (2005) urges prohibition; scientific + ethical concerns. INDIA: Dept of Biotech policy bans human reproductive cloning. No country currently allows reproductive human cloning. DOLLY LEGACY: (1) proved adult cells can be REPROGRAMMED — earlier thought impossible after differentiation. (2) paved way for IPSCs (Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells — Shinya YAMANAKA 2006, Nobel 2012) — adult cells reprogrammed to stem-cell state via 4 factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc — 'Yamanaka factors'). Avoid ethical issues of embryonic stem cells. (3) Enabled stem cell therapies + regenerative medicine research. (4) Agricultural livestock multiplication (cloning elite cattle, pigs). INDIAN CONTEXT: National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI, Karnal) cloned first buffalo 'GARIMA' (2009) + 'GARIMA-II' (2011). Several buffalo clones of top milk producers. Mesenchymal stem cell research + CAR-T cell therapy at AIIMS + Tata Memorial (2024 India approved 1st indigenous CAR-T for cancer 'NexCAR19'). EMBRYO CLONING for infertility + GM animals + gene drives + ecological applications — active research globally.

questions.stem: The COMMON ANCESTOR of humans + chimpanzees lived approximately:

options.option_text: 6-7 MILLION years ago — Sahelanthropus + Orrorin + Ardipithecus are candidates; human + chimp DNA ~98.8% identical

questions.explanation: LAST COMMON ANCESTOR (LCA) of humans + chimpanzees (+ bonobos) lived ~6-7 MILLION YEARS AGO in AFRICA. After LCA, lineages diverged: (a) human lineage → hominins → eventually HOMO SAPIENS; (b) chimp lineage → Pan troglodytes (common chimp) + Pan paniscus (bonobo, diverged ~1-2 Mya). DNA SIMILARITY: humans + chimps share ~98.8% of their DNA (protein-coding sequences; ~98% overall including introns). Just 1.2% difference (~35 million bp). Still 99%+ similar at protein level. HUMAN vs CHIMP physical differences: (a) BIPEDALISM (humans) vs knuckle-walking; (b) LESS HAIR (humans); (c) LARGER brain (human 1350 cc vs chimp 350 cc); (d) SMALLER teeth, jaw; (e) FULL RANGE of VERBAL LANGUAGE (chimps limited); (f) OPPOSABLE thumb with longer reach (humans better precision grip); (g) forming COMPLEX SOCIETIES with abstract thought + technology. EARLY HOMININ CANDIDATES (post-LCA): (1) SAHELANTHROPUS TCHADENSIS — Chad, 6-7 MYA; 'Toumai' skull 2001 (Michel Brunet). Possibly first bipedal hominin. Debated whether truly human lineage or chimp ancestor. (2) ORRORIN TUGENENSIS — Kenya 6 MYA; 'Millennium Man' 2000. (3) ARDIPITHECUS RAMIDUS — Ethiopia 4.4 MYA; 'Ardi' fossil (Tim White 1994, published 2009) — bipedal + arboreal. (4) AUSTRALOPITHECUS AFARENSIS — 3.9-2.9 MYA; 'LUCY' 1974 Johanson, Ethiopia (40% complete skeleton; named after Beatles' 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds' playing in camp). Bipedal. (5) HOMO emerged ~2.5 MYA — H. habilis first. EVIDENCE for COMMON ANCESTRY: (1) ANATOMICAL — humans + chimps share 400+ bones in same pattern + 206 same. (2) GENETIC — DNA similarity; CHROMOSOMAL FUSION — humans have 23 pairs, chimps 24; Chromosome 2 in humans = fusion of 2 ancestral chimp chromosomes (remnant TELOMERES + CENTROMERE visible in human Chr 2 — strong evidence). (3) BEHAVIOURAL — tool use (chimps use sticks + stones), social structures, ALLIANCES, simple symbolic comm, self-recognition in mirror (some chimps pass 'mirror test' like humans + dolphins + elephants + magpies). (4) BIOCHEMICAL — similar hemoglobins, cytochromes, digestive enzymes. (5) DEVELOPMENTAL — embryos nearly indistinguishable at early stages. JANE GOODALL's landmark chimp studies (Gombe Tanzania 1960-present) changed understanding: chimps use TOOLS, HUNT cooperatively, wage WAR (Gombe Chimpanzee War 1974-78), show cultural variation across populations, have emotions. BONOBOS — discovered 1928 as separate species; matriarchal, peaceful society with sex as conflict resolution; sexually liberal. DNA ratio: humans:chimps:bonobos ~98.8:98.8% (triad; some genes more chimp-like in human, others more bonobo-like). NEANDERTHAL-HUMAN DNA: non-African modern humans have 1-4% Neanderthal DNA (from interbreeding 50-65k ya). DENISOVAN DNA: Melanesians + some Asians have 3-6% Denisovan DNA.

questions.stem: THEORY OF EVOLUTION that emphasises GRADUAL changes over long periods is:

options.option_text: GRADUALISM (Darwin-Wallace original) — small changes accumulate over millions of years; vs 'PUNCTUATED EQUILIBRIUM' (Eldredge + Gould, 1972) — rapid speciation separated by long stasis

questions.explanation: THEORIES of EVOLUTION — multiple historical + ongoing debates: (1) LAMARCKISM (Jean-Baptiste LAMARCK 1809) — first coherent evolution theory; INHERITANCE of ACQUIRED CHARACTERS. Organisms adapt during life (e.g., GIRAFFE stretches neck to reach high leaves) + pass acquired trait to offspring. 'USE + DISUSE' — used organs develop, unused ones atrophy. REJECTED by modern biology (August Weismann's Germplasm theory 1880s — rat tail amputations didn't lead to tailless offspring for 22 generations). EPIGENETICS has partially rehabilitated Lamarck's idea — some ACQUIRED DNA methylation + histone marks CAN be inherited for 1-2 generations; but NOT full Lamarckian mechanisms. (2) DARWINISM / NATURAL SELECTION (Darwin + Wallace 1858-59) — gradual heritable variations in populations, selection by environment → evolution. Emphasised GRADUALISM — small changes over millions of years. (3) MUTATIONISM (Hugo de Vries 1900s) — evolution driven by SUDDEN MUTATIONS (large jumps). Key part of modern synthesis but not alone. (4) MODERN SYNTHESIS / NEO-DARWINISM (1930s-40s) — Darwin + Mendel unified. Fisher, Haldane, Sewall Wright — mathematics of population genetics. Dobzhansky, Mayr, Simpson, Huxley, Stebbins — unified genetics + paleontology + systematics + botany. Evolution = changes in ALLELE FREQUENCIES in populations over time. Mechanisms: (a) NATURAL SELECTION; (b) GENETIC DRIFT (random fluctuations, strong in small pops); (c) MUTATION (source of variation); (d) GENE FLOW (migration); (e) non-random mating. HARDY-WEINBERG EQUILIBRIUM describes no-evolution baseline. (5) NEUTRAL THEORY (Motoo Kimura 1968) — most molecular evolution is NEUTRAL (random drift of mutations that neither benefit nor harm). Explains molecular clock + neutrality at DNA level. (6) PUNCTUATED EQUILIBRIUM (Niles ELDREDGE + Stephen Jay GOULD 1972) — evolution not gradual but proceeds in RAPID BURSTS of speciation separated by LONG PERIODS of STASIS. Based on fossil record — transitions often abrupt. Compatible with Darwinism. (7) EVO-DEVO (Evolutionary Developmental Biology, 1980s-present) — small changes in DEVELOPMENTAL REGULATORY GENES (Hox genes etc.) produce large morphological changes. Explains body plans + adaptations. (8) KIN SELECTION + GROUP SELECTION (Hamilton 1964; Williams; Wilson) — altruism evolves via gene sharing among relatives ('inclusive fitness'). (9) SEXUAL SELECTION (Darwin 1871) — traits that enhance mate attraction (peacock's tail, deer antlers, bird songs, human aesthetics) — even if survival-costly. (10) ENDOSYMBIOTIC THEORY (Lynn Margulis 1967) — mitochondria + chloroplasts arose from engulfed bacteria living symbiotically inside early eukaryotes. Universally accepted. (11) HORIZONTAL GENE TRANSFER — between species, common in bacteria + some eukaryotes; complicates tree of life. Recent additions + refinements: (a) multi-level selection (Wilson); (b) niche construction; (c) epigenetic inheritance; (d) development drives evolution; (e) quantum evolution (debated). COMMON CREATIONIST/ID claims + scientific responses: evolution is 'just a theory' (theory = well-supported framework; evolution is FACT + theory), missing links (plenty found), irreducible complexity (Behe; refuted by flagellum evolution examples; Dover v. Kitzmiller 2005 legal ruling rejected ID as science). EVOLUTION is a bedrock of modern biology — medical, agricultural, ecological applications.
